KM1Zj77x6jyW9VsInPz3.description:
Ralligold GR from Tata Rallis is a granular mycorrhizal biofertilizer. Mycorrhizal fungi live on plant roots and spread fine threads into the soil, so the crop can reach phosphorus, water and micronutrients that its own roots cannot. The result farmers look for is a stronger root system, better use of the fertilizer already applied, and a crop that copes better with dry spells.

Because it is a granule, Ralligold GR goes into the soil near the root zone: at sowing or transplanting, or along the rows in standing crops, mixed with sand, soil or compost so it spreads evenly. It suits most field crops, vegetables and fruit crops, including tomato, chilli, potato, cotton, maize, wheat, onion, soybean, pulses, sugarcane, ginger, turmeric, banana, grapes, pomegranate and citrus.

As a biological product it works best in moist soil with organic matter. Keep the pack sealed in a cool, shaded place and use it before the expiry date printed on the bag, since the fungal spores are alive.

faqs.q: How much Ralligold GR should I use per acre?
faqs.a: The seller's listing gives 4 kg per acre for most field crops and vegetables, and 8 kg per acre for long-duration crops such as sugarcane, ginger, turmeric and banana. Follow the rate on your pack, as it can differ by crop.
At sowing or transplanting, placed close to the seed or root zone, or along the rows early in the crop. The fungi need to reach young roots to colonise them.

faqs.q: Can I mix Ralligold GR with chemical fertilizers?
faqs.a: It can go into soil that has received normal fertilizer, but do not mix it in the same bag or tank with fungicides, which can harm the living fungi. Apply fungicide seed treatments and soil drenches separately.

faqs.q: Is it the same as a phosphate fertilizer?
faqs.a: No. It adds no phosphorus itself; it helps roots take up the phosphorus that is already in the soil or that you apply.

jhXloji8VeTbqLwNku3c.description:
Adama 2,4-D is a selective, systemic herbicide based on 2,4-D, one of the most widely used weed killers for broadleaf weeds. It is absorbed through the leaves, moves through the weed and disturbs its growth hormones, so susceptible weeds twist, stop growing and die over one to two weeks. Grasses and cereal crops are much less sensitive to it, which is why 2,4-D is used to clean broadleaf weeds out of crops such as wheat, maize, sorghum and sugarcane.

Spray it after the weeds have emerged and while they are young and actively growing. Use a flat-fan nozzle, spray on a calm day, and keep the spray away from sensitive broadleaf crops such as cotton, tomato, chilli, grapes and pulses: even a little drift can damage them.

The dose and the right crop stage are printed on the label for each crop. Wear gloves and a mask while mixing and spraying, and do not use the same pump for insecticide or fungicide sprays on sensitive crops without washing it thoroughly.

faqs.a: Broadleaf weeds such as Chenopodium (bathua), Convolvulus, Parthenium and many other dicot weeds. It does not control grassy weeds.

faqs.q: In which crops can I use it?
faqs.a: In crops where it is registered on the label, typically cereals such as wheat and maize, and sugarcane. Never spray it on cotton, vegetables, pulses or fruit crops.
Follow the crop-specific dose and water volume on the Adama label. The rate depends on the crop and the weed stage.

faqs.q: How soon will I see results?
faqs.a: Leaves start to curl and twist within a few days; weeds usually die in one to two weeks.

CtVwXhQFGN30lyRraK1X.description:
Alika from Syngenta is an insecticide that combines two actives: thiamethoxam 12.6% and lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% in a ZC (mixed capsule suspension) formulation. Thiamethoxam is systemic: the plant takes it up and it protects new growth against sucking pests such as jassids, aphids, whiteflies and thrips. Lambda-cyhalothrin acts on contact and gives a quick knockdown of chewing pests such as caterpillars and bollworms.

That pairing makes Alika useful when a crop has sucking and chewing pests at the same time, for example in cotton, maize, soybean, chilli and tomato. The ZC formulation releases part of the lambda-cyhalothrin quickly and part over time, so control lasts longer than with a simple EC.

Spray at the first sign of pest build-up, with good coverage of both leaf surfaces. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the Syngenta label, and avoid spraying when bees are active, as both actives are toxic to bees.

faqs.a: Thiamethoxam 12.6% plus lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% ZC.
Sucking pests such as jassids, aphids, thrips and whiteflies, and chewing pests such as caterpillars and bollworms, in the crops listed on its label.

faqs.q: What is the dose per acre?
faqs.a: It depends on the crop. Follow the dose, water volume and waiting period printed on the Syngenta label for your crop.
No. Both actives are toxic to bees. Do not spray on flowering crops while bees are foraging; spray in the evening if needed.

dC3JogwQI7uGAORqApuM.description:
Fusiflex from Syngenta is a selective post-emergence herbicide for soybean and other broadleaf crops. It combines two actives that cover each other's gaps: fluazifop-p-butyl, which kills grassy weeds by stopping fat production in the grass, and fomesafen, which burns down broadleaf weeds by disrupting their cell membranes. One spray therefore controls both grasses and broadleaf weeds in the crop.

The best time to spray is when the weeds are young, at the two to four leaf stage, and the crop is in its early growth. Use clean water and a flat-fan nozzle for even cover, and do not spray before rain. Fusiflex is used in soybean in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, where it is one of the common weed-control sprays in kharif.

Use the dose and water volume given on the Syngenta label, and do not spray it on cereal crops such as maize, wheat or rice, which are grasses and will be damaged.

faqs.a: Mainly soybean, and other broadleaf crops listed on its label. It must not be used on maize, wheat, rice or other cereal crops.
Grassy weeds such as Echinochloa and Digitaria, and broadleaf weeds such as Commelina, Digera and Amaranthus, when sprayed at the young stage.
Post-emergence, when weeds have two to four leaves. Older weeds are harder to kill.
Follow the dose and water volume printed on the Syngenta label for your crop.

PvvTdzZEvxaBEIUyirrR.description:
Tata Metri from Rallis India contains metribuzin 70% WP, a selective systemic herbicide. Metribuzin is taken up by both roots and leaves and blocks photosynthesis in susceptible weeds, which turn yellow and die. It controls many annual broadleaf weeds and some annual grasses, and it is used in crops such as soybean, potato, tomato, wheat and sugarcane, depending on the label.

Metribuzin can be applied before the weeds come up (pre-emergence) or soon after (early post-emergence), as the label for each crop specifies. Applied to moist soil, it forms a weed-free layer that stops new flushes for several weeks. Light, sandy soils with little organic matter need extra care, because the active moves faster and can harm the crop.

The 100 g pack suits small plots. Mix the powder in a little water first, then fill the tank. Follow the crop-specific dose and timing on the Rallis label, and wear gloves and a mask while mixing.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Tata Metri?
faqs.a: Metribuzin 70% WP (wettable powder).

faqs.q: In which crops can Tata Metri be used?
faqs.a: In the crops listed on its label, such as soybean, potato, tomato, wheat and sugarcane. Check the label before using it on any other crop.

faqs.q: Should I spray it before or after the weeds come up?
faqs.a: It works as a pre-emergence or early post-emergence herbicide depending on the crop. Follow the timing on the label for your crop.
It depends on the crop and soil type. Use the dose on the Rallis label; lower rates are usually advised on light soils.

Hy4dLsiPmHkHfCTDHYtX.description:
Weedmar Super from Dhanuka is a selective post-emergence herbicide containing 2,4-D amine salt 58% SL. It controls broadleaf weeds and sedges in cereal crops and sugarcane. The amine salt is absorbed through the leaves and moves through the weed to its growing points, where it upsets the plant's hormone balance; affected weeds twist, stop growing and die over one to two weeks.

Weedmar Super is commonly used in wheat, maize, sorghum, rice and sugarcane to clean up broadleaf weeds such as bathua (Chenopodium), Convolvulus and Parthenium, and sedges such as Cyperus. Spray when the weeds are young and actively growing, on a calm day, with a flat-fan nozzle.

Keep it well away from broadleaf crops such as cotton, vegetables, grapes and pulses, which are very sensitive to 2,4-D drift. Follow the dose and timing printed on the Dhanuka label for your crop.

faqs.a: 2,4-D amine salt 58% SL.

faqs.q: Which crops can I spray it on?
faqs.a: Cereal crops such as wheat, maize, sorghum and rice, and sugarcane, as listed on the label.
No. It controls broadleaf weeds and sedges. Grassy weeds need a different herbicide.

faqs.q: Is it safe near cotton or vegetables?
faqs.a: No. Even small amounts of drift can damage cotton, vegetables, grapes and pulses. Spray only on calm days and keep a safe distance.

wrhEtw0k4nvEypl7EkUt.description:
Tizom is a sugarcane herbicide from Dhanuka Agritech, developed with Nissan Chemical Corporation of Japan and launched in 2023. It combines halosulfuron methyl 6% and metribuzin 50% WG. Halosulfuron is one of the few actives that reliably controls motha (Cyperus rotundus, nutsedge), the hardest weed in sugarcane, while metribuzin takes care of broadleaf weeds and grasses.

Tizom is a selective, systemic, post-emergence herbicide: it is sprayed after the weeds have come up, and the cane is not harmed when it is used as the label directs. One spray covers narrow-leaf weeds, broadleaf weeds and nutsedge together, and the combination keeps the field clean for longer than either active alone.

Spray when the weeds are young and actively growing, with enough water for good cover. Tizom was launched first in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Follow the dose and timing on the Dhanuka label.

faqs.a: Halosulfuron methyl 6% plus metribuzin 50% WG.
Sugarcane.
Yes. Halosulfuron methyl in Tizom controls Cyperus rotundus (motha), along with broadleaf and grassy weeds.
Post-emergence, when the weeds are young and actively growing. Follow the timing and dose on the Dhanuka label.

hPfubvUUkHn4WIh1mYLb.description:
Sempra from Dhanuka contains halosulfuron methyl 75% WG, a selective herbicide made for one of the toughest weeds in Indian fields: motha, or nutsedge (Cyperus rotundus). Motha regrows from underground tubers, so cutting or hoeing only brings it back. Halosulfuron is absorbed by the leaves and moves down to the tubers, stopping the weed from regrowing.

Sempra is used in sugarcane and maize, where it is sprayed after the weeds have come up. It is a very concentrated granule, which is why the packs are small: 18 g and 36 g. Dissolve it fully in a little water before adding it to the tank, and add a surfactant only if the label asks for it.

Spray when motha is at the three to five leaf stage and actively growing; very dry weather slows the effect. Visible yellowing takes a week or more, and full control two to three weeks. Follow the dose and crop list on the Dhanuka label.

faqs.a: Mainly motha (nutsedge, Cyperus rotundus), including regrowth from its tubers.

faqs.q: In which crops can I use Sempra?
faqs.a: Sugarcane and maize, as listed on the label.

faqs.q: Why is the pack so small?
faqs.a: Halosulfuron methyl 75% WG is highly concentrated, so only a few grams are needed per acre. Follow the label dose.

faqs.q: How long does it take to work?
faqs.a: The weed stops growing quickly; yellowing shows in about a week and full control in two to three weeks.

crdWl9x2nxWByhoxoPf4.description:
Gluco Potash-X from SuvarnaBhumi is a liquid potassium nutrient containing 22% potassium gluconate. Gluconate is an organic carrier: it helps potassium enter the leaf quickly when sprayed and moves easily inside the plant. This makes it useful as a foliar spray at the stages when crops need extra potassium most, such as flowering, fruit filling and grain filling.

Potassium controls water use in the plant, builds sugar and starch in fruits and grains, and strengthens cell walls. Crops with enough potassium have better fruit size, colour, shine and keeping quality, and stand up better to drought and disease. It is used in vegetables, fruit crops such as grapes, pomegranate and banana, and field crops.

Gluco Potash is a fertilizer, not a pesticide. It can usually be sprayed with water-soluble fertilizers; test a small mix first before adding it to pesticide sprays. Follow the dose on the pack for your crop stage.

faqs.a: 22% potassium gluconate in liquid form, according to the listing.
From flowering through fruit or grain development, when the crop's need for potassium is highest.
No. It is a potassium fertilizer for foliar feeding. It does not control pests or diseases.
Vegetables, fruit crops such as grapes, pomegranate and banana, and field crops, especially where fruit size and quality matter.

9qg6pmBO8DsAJ92TnDfj.description:
Karate from Syngenta contains lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC, a synthetic pyrethroid insecticide. It acts on contact and through ingestion, attacking the insect's nervous system, which gives a fast knockdown of chewing and some sucking pests. Lambda-cyhalothrin also has a repellent effect, so treated plants are less attractive to pests for some days after spraying.

Karate is used against bollworms, caterpillars, leaf folders, stem borers, jassids and thrips in crops such as cotton, rice, chilli, tomato, brinjal and pulses, depending on the label. Because it acts on contact, coverage matters: spray both sides of the leaves, and spray at the first sign of the pest rather than after damage has spread.

Pyrethroids should be rotated with insecticides from other groups to avoid resistance. Karate is toxic to fish and bees, so keep it away from ponds and avoid spraying flowering crops when bees are active. Follow the dose and waiting period on the Syngenta label.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Karate?
faqs.a: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC.
Chewing pests such as bollworms, caterpillars, stem borers and leaf folders, and some sucking pests such as jassids and thrips, in the crops on its label.

faqs.q: How often can I spray it?
faqs.a: Follow the number of sprays and waiting period on the label, and rotate with insecticides from other groups to prevent resistance.

faqs.q: Is Karate harmful to bees and fish?
faqs.a: Yes. Avoid spraying flowering crops while bees forage, and keep it away from ponds, canals and wells.

Hhf1qiBLdQgeC74Bndld.description:
Ridomil Gold from Syngenta is a fungicide for downy mildew, late blight and other diseases caused by oomycete pathogens (Phytophthora, Pythium, Peronospora and similar). The widely sold Ridomil Gold MZ combines metalaxyl-M, a systemic active that moves inside the plant and stops infection that has already started, with mancozeb, a contact active that protects the leaf surface against new infection.

It is used in potato and tomato against late blight, in grapes and cucurbits against downy mildew, and in other crops listed on the label. Apply it preventively when weather favours disease (cool nights, dew, cloudy humid days) or at the first symptoms. The systemic part gives a curative effect for a short time after infection; the contact part keeps protecting the leaf.

To keep metalaxyl-M effective, do not spray it again and again: use it two or three times a season at most, and alternate with fungicides from other groups. Follow the dose and crop list on the Syngenta label.

faqs.q: Which diseases does Ridomil Gold control?
faqs.a: Diseases caused by oomycetes: late blight of potato and tomato, downy mildew of grapes and cucurbits, and others listed on the label.
Both. Metalaxyl-M is systemic and mancozeb is contact, so it protects the leaf and acts inside the plant.
Before or at the first sign of disease, especially in cool, humid weather. Follow the label for spray intervals.

faqs.q: Can I use it all season?
faqs.a: Limit it to two or three sprays a season and alternate with other fungicide groups so the disease does not become resistant.

iTx1bO0gnZHhKZ301Nnt.description:
Topas from Syngenta contains penconazole 10% EC, a systemic triazole fungicide best known for controlling powdery mildew. Penconazole is absorbed by the leaves and moves upward in the plant, protecting new growth as well as the sprayed surface. It stops the fungus building its cell membranes, which halts both new infection and the spread of patches already present.

Topas is widely used on grapes, and on vegetables and fruit crops such as chilli, mango, apple and cucurbits where powdery mildew is a problem, depending on the label. The white, powdery patches on leaves, shoots or fruit are the sign to act; early sprays at the first patches work far better than late ones.

Because it is concentrated, the dose per litre is small, so measure carefully. Rotate Topas with fungicides from other groups to avoid resistance, and follow the dose, spray interval and waiting period on the Syngenta label.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Topas?
faqs.a: Penconazole 10% EC.
Mainly powdery mildew, in crops such as grapes, chilli, mango and cucurbits as listed on the label.
Yes. It is absorbed by the leaves and moves upward, protecting new growth.
Follow the dose and spray interval on the Syngenta label for your crop; measure carefully, as the rate per litre is small.

PRAA5LU6vXxyQbLd6TYy.description:
Kavach Flo from Syngenta is a contact fungicide based on chlorothalonil, in a flowable liquid formulation that mixes easily in the tank. Chlorothalonil forms a protective layer on the leaf and kills fungal spores as they germinate. It acts at many sites in the fungus at once, so resistance to it is very rare, which makes it a reliable partner to rotate with systemic fungicides.

Kavach Flo is used against leaf spots, early blight, anthracnose, fruit rots and similar diseases in crops such as potato, tomato, chilli, groundnut and fruit crops, as listed on the label. Being a contact fungicide, it protects only what it covers: spray before disease sets in or at the very first spots, and repeat at the interval on the label, especially after rain.

Note that Kavach Flo is a fungicide, not a fertilizer. Follow the dose and waiting period on the Syngenta label, and wear gloves and eye protection while mixing.

faqs.a: A chlorothalonil-based contact fungicide from Syngenta in a flowable formulation. It is not a fertilizer.
Leaf spots, early blight, anthracnose, fruit rots and other fungal diseases on the crops listed on its label.
Preventively, before disease appears or at the first spots, and again at the label interval, especially after rain.

faqs.q: Can I rotate it with systemic fungicides?
faqs.a: Yes. Chlorothalonil acts at many sites in the fungus, so it is a good rotation partner that helps prevent resistance.

6Mv6T9TVuBm3YVmS7J6O.description:
Nano Urea is IFFCO's liquid nitrogen fertilizer, made with nitrogen in nano-particle form. It is sprayed on the leaves instead of being spread on the soil. The tiny particles enter through the leaf pores and release nitrogen inside the plant, so much less nitrogen is lost to the air or washed out of the soil than with granular urea.

IFFCO recommends Nano Urea as a foliar spray at the stages when the crop needs nitrogen most: usually one spray at active tillering or branching, and a second before flowering. It is used in cereals such as wheat, rice and maize, in pulses, oilseeds, cotton, vegetables and fruit crops. Farmers use it to replace part of the top-dressed granular urea; the basal dose of nitrogen still goes into the soil.

Shake the bottle well, spray in the morning or evening when the leaf pores are open, and avoid spraying just before rain. A 500 ml bottle covers about one acre for one spray.

faqs.q: How do I use Nano Urea?
faqs.a: IFFCO recommends 2–4 ml per litre of water as a foliar spray, at active growth and again before flowering. Follow the instructions on the bottle.

faqs.q: Can Nano Urea fully replace granular urea?
faqs.a: No. It replaces part of the top-dressed urea. The basal nitrogen dose at sowing should still be applied to the soil.

faqs.q: How much area does one bottle cover?
faqs.a: One 500 ml bottle is meant for about one acre per spray.

faqs.q: When is the best time of day to spray?
faqs.a: Early morning or evening, when the leaf pores are open and the spray does not dry too fast. Avoid spraying if rain is expected within a few hours.

xMZfZAkpnXzV2m3WWrIH.description:
Kazoo is a plant nutrient containing ortho silicic acid (OSA) 2.0% WSL, the form of silicon that plants can absorb directly. Soil contains plenty of silicon, but mostly in forms roots cannot take up; ortho silicic acid is ready to use. Silicon builds up in the cell walls of leaves and stems, making them stronger and more upright.

Stronger tissue helps the crop in several ways: leaves stand better and catch more light, stems lodge less, the plant loses less water in dry spells, and the hard layer makes it harder for sucking pests and fungal spores to get in. Silicon also helps the plant handle heat and salt stress, and supports better uptake of other nutrients. Kazoo is used in fruits, vegetables, flowers and field crops such as rice, sugarcane and wheat.

It is applied as a foliar spray or through drip at the vegetative and flowering stages. Follow the dose on the pack for your crop.

faqs.a: Ortho silicic acid (OSA) 2.0% WSL, a plant-available form of silicon.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of silicon for crops?
faqs.a: Stronger leaves and stems, less lodging, better tolerance to drought, heat and salt stress, and a tougher barrier against sucking pests and fungal infection.
As a foliar spray or through drip irrigation, at the vegetative and flowering stages. Follow the dose on the pack.
Fruits, vegetables, flowers and field crops such as rice, sugarcane and wheat.

Khnn66dLVddRPT4TZ2TU.description:
Karan Veer is a liquid biostimulant from Hifield Organics containing 20% plant-source protein hydrolysate. Protein hydrolysates are proteins broken down into amino acids and short peptides. Plants absorb these quickly through leaves and roots and use them as building blocks, so the crop saves the energy it would spend making them itself.

The effect is strongest at demanding stages: flowering, fruit set and fruit development, and recovery after stress such as heat, cold, waterlogging or a heavy pesticide spray. Amino acids also help the plant take up and use other nutrients, which is why biostimulants like Karan Veer are often sprayed together with water-soluble fertilizers. It suits vegetables, fruit crops and field crops.

Karan Veer comes in 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre packs. Spray it on the leaves or apply through drip at the growth stages where you want the push, and follow the dose on the pack.

faqs.a: 20% protein hydrolysate from plant sources (amino acids and peptides).
Before and during flowering, at fruit set and fruit development, and to help the crop recover after stress.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with fertilizers?
faqs.a: It is commonly sprayed with water-soluble fertilizers. Test a small mix first before adding pesticides to the same tank.
As a foliar spray or through drip irrigation. Follow the dose on the pack.

5cg6cDoHI3B5yXTLCU8S.description:
Amaze XL is a plant growth stimulant made from seaweed extract and amino acids. Seaweed extracts carry natural plant growth substances and trace elements, while amino acids are ready-made building blocks the plant can use straight away. Together they support flowering, fruit setting, greener leaves and steady growth.

Farmers use Amaze XL at the stages where the crop needs a push: during vegetative growth, before and during flowering, and at fruit set, and after stress such as heat, cold or a heavy spray. Because it is a nutrition and growth product, it can be used alongside the normal fertilizer schedule; it does not replace NPK. It suits vegetables, fruit crops, flowers and field crops.

Amaze XL is available in 250 ml and 500 ml packs. Apply it as a foliar spray in the morning or evening, and follow the dose given on the pack for your crop.

faqs.q: What is Amaze XL made of?
faqs.a: Seaweed extract and amino acids.

faqs.q: What does it do for the crop?
faqs.a: It supports flowering, fruit setting, leaf greenness and growth, and helps the crop recover from stress.
No. It is a growth stimulant. It does not control pests or diseases.
During vegetative growth, before and during flowering, and at fruit set. Follow the dose on the pack.

ra5xPnPeXNZAelOZtEOF.description:
AS 712 is a hybrid maize (corn) seed bred for high yield and good grain quality. Hybrid maize gives uniform plants with strong vigour and well-filled, even cobs, which is what both grain buyers and poultry-feed traders look for. AS 712 is suited to both kharif and rabi seasons, which gives farmers flexibility in planning.

For the best results, sow in well-prepared, well-drained soil with good organic matter, at the spacing advised on the seed pack. Maize responds strongly to nitrogen and needs it at knee height and before tasselling, along with phosphorus and potassium at sowing. Keep the field free of weeds for the first 30 to 40 days, and watch for fall armyworm in the early whorl stage.

Hybrid seed should be bought fresh each season; seed saved from a hybrid crop does not give the same yield. Each 4 kg pack is treated and graded for good germination.

faqs.q: Which season is AS 712 suitable for?
faqs.a: Both kharif and rabi, according to the listing.

faqs.q: Can I save seed from my AS 712 crop to sow next season?
faqs.a: No. Seed from a hybrid crop does not give the same uniformity or yield. Buy fresh seed each season.

faqs.q: What is the main pest to watch for?
faqs.a: Fall armyworm in the early whorl stage. Check the whorls regularly from emergence and act early.
Maize needs nitrogen in splits (at sowing, knee height and before tasselling) plus phosphorus and potassium at sowing. Follow a soil test where possible.

alXNM9Y3wtuZqJib7BDd.description:
Amistar Top from Syngenta is a broad-spectrum systemic fungicide combining azoxystrobin 18.2% and difenoconazole 11.4% SC. Azoxystrobin stops the fungus from producing energy and has strong preventive action; difenoconazole stops it building its cell membranes and adds curative action against infections that have already started. Using two modes of action also lowers the risk of resistance.

Amistar Top controls blights, leaf spots, rusts, powdery mildew, sheath blight and similar diseases in crops such as rice, wheat, maize, cotton, tomato, chilli, onion, turmeric and sugarcane, as listed on the label. It is absorbed into the leaf and spreads within it, so it keeps working even after light rain once the spray has dried.

Spray at the first signs of disease, or preventively when the weather favours it. The seller's listing gives 200 ml per acre, subject to the crop-specific label. Use enough water for full coverage, and follow the spray interval and waiting period on the Syngenta label.

faqs.a: Azoxystrobin 18.2% plus difenoconazole 11.4% SC.
The listing gives 200 ml per acre, subject to the crop-specific directions on the Syngenta label.
Blights, leaf spots, rusts, powdery mildew, sheath blight and other fungal diseases on the crops listed on its label.
Both. Azoxystrobin is mainly preventive and difenoconazole adds curative action against early infection.

QlsamDYSLYKhFgnr64rj.description:
Clavengo is a non-selective herbicide containing glufosinate ammonium 13.5% SL. It kills almost any green weed it touches, grassy or broadleaf, by blocking an enzyme the plant needs to process ammonia. Ammonia builds up inside the leaf, and the weed dries out quickly, usually within a few days.

Glufosinate acts mainly on contact and moves only a little within the plant, so good coverage is important: spray all green parts of the weeds evenly. It is used to clear weeds before sowing, along field bunds, in orchards and plantations, and between rows of crops using a hood or shield so the spray does not touch the crop. Being non-selective, it will damage any crop leaves it lands on.

Clavengo comes in 500 ml and 1 litre packs. Spray on a calm day when the weeds are actively growing, and avoid spraying just before rain. Follow the dose and uses on the label.

faqs.a: Glufosinate ammonium 13.5% SL.
Yes, if the spray touches it. It is non-selective. Use it before sowing, on bunds and in orchards, or between rows with a shield.
Weeds usually dry out within a few days of spraying.

faqs.q: How is it different from glyphosate?
faqs.a: Glufosinate acts faster but mostly on contact, so it needs good coverage; glyphosate is slower but moves to the roots.

spxjewbVyEoGw9xBtMKM.description:
Amipro-K is a liquid phosphorus and potassium fertilizer made for quick uptake through the leaves or the drip line. It is fully soluble and free of sodium and chlorine, which matters for crops that are sensitive to salt, and it delivers nutrients in a form the plant can use straight away, so small doses go a long way.

Phosphorus supports root growth, flowering and energy transfer in the plant; potassium builds fruit size, sugar content, colour and keeping quality, and helps the plant manage water. A P and K feed like Amipro-K is used mainly from flowering through fruit development, and to support root growth after transplanting. It suits vegetables, fruit crops such as grapes, pomegranate and banana, and field crops.

Amipro-K is a fertilizer, not a pesticide, even though it may be filed with crop protection products in some lists. Apply it as a foliar spray or through drip, and follow the dose on the pack for your crop stage.

faqs.a: Phosphorus and potassium in a fully soluble liquid form, free of sodium and chlorine.
Mainly from flowering through fruit development, and after transplanting to support root growth.
As a foliar spray or through drip irrigation. Follow the dose on the pack.
No. It is a fertilizer and does not control pests or diseases.

ogbzRDaOODZx65b4F65M.description:
Trust from NACL Industries contains emamectin benzoate 5% SG, an insecticide made for caterpillars. Emamectin benzoate is taken in by the larva when it feeds on treated leaves; within hours the caterpillar stops feeding and is paralysed, and it dies over the next two to four days. It also penetrates the leaf (translaminar action), so caterpillars feeding on the underside are reached too.

Trust is used against fruit borers, shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth, armyworms and other caterpillar pests in crops such as chilli, tomato, brinjal, okra, cabbage, onion and maize, as listed on the label. It works best on young larvae, so spray when you first see eggs hatching or early feeding damage.

It is a soluble granule: dissolve it in a little water before adding it to the tank. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the NACL label, and rotate with insecticides from other groups.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Trust?
faqs.a: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG.
Caterpillar pests such as fruit and shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth and armyworms on the crops listed on its label.

faqs.q: Does it control sucking pests like whitefly?
faqs.a: No. Emamectin benzoate is made for caterpillars. Sucking pests need a different insecticide.
When young larvae appear or early feeding damage is seen. It works best on young caterpillars.

1gFATYy3y81N4lf3y98U.description:
AS 771 is a hybrid maize seed produced and processed for high germination, genetic purity and field performance. The seed is cleaned and graded to remove inert matter and weed seeds, and the listing gives a germination rate of 90%. Uniform seed gives an even stand, which is the base for even cobs and a good harvest.

Sow AS 771 in well-drained, well-prepared soil at the spacing on the seed pack. Maize needs nitrogen in splits (at sowing, at knee height and before tasselling) with phosphorus and potassium at sowing, and enough water at tasselling and silking, when stress hurts yield most. Keep the field weed-free for the first five to six weeks.

Scout the young crop for fall armyworm in the whorls and act early if you see feeding holes. Hybrid seed should be bought fresh each season. Each pack holds 4 kg.

faqs.q: What is the germination rate of AS 771?
faqs.a: The listing states 90%.
Yes. Buy fresh seed each season; seed saved from the crop will not perform the same.

faqs.q: When does maize need water most?
faqs.a: At tasselling and silking. Water stress at this stage reduces grain filling the most.

faqs.q: How do I protect it from fall armyworm?
faqs.a: Check the whorls of young plants regularly from emergence and spray at the first sign of feeding, following a registered product's label.

QTrGz1Xz6xsYvRv7q9i4.description:
NPK 11:11:8 from R. M. Phosphates & Chemicals (RMPCL) is a water-soluble suspension fertilizer with balanced nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, fortified with micronutrients. The liquid suspension format lets the nutrients reach the plant quickly through a foliar spray, and the added micronutrients help correct hidden deficiencies that hold back growth even when NPK is enough.

With nitrogen and phosphorus in equal parts and a little less potassium, the 11:11:8 grade suits the early and middle stages of the crop: vegetative growth, root building and branching. It is used in vegetables, field crops and fruit crops as a supplement to soil-applied fertilizer, especially when the crop needs a quick push or the soil is dry and roots cannot take up nutrients well.

Shake the bottle well before use, spray in the morning or evening, and follow the dose given on the pack. Test a small mix first if you want to combine it with pesticides.

faqs.a: It contains 11% nitrogen, 11% phosphorus (as P2O5) and 8% potassium (as K2O), plus added micronutrients.

faqs.q: At what stage should I use it?
faqs.a: During early and middle growth: vegetative growth, root development and branching.
No. It supplements the basal fertilizer, giving the crop a quick boost through the leaves.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with pesticides?
faqs.a: Often yes, but test a small mix first to check that nothing settles or curdles.

DODXqry30vXvk4Yjax5Q.description:
Rosentra from Syngenta India contains topramezone 336 g/L (w/v) SC, a selective post-emergence herbicide for maize. Topramezone belongs to the triketone group of HPPD inhibitors: it blocks an enzyme the weed needs to make protective pigments, so new leaves turn white (bleach) in sunlight and the weed dies within one to two weeks. Maize breaks down topramezone quickly, which is why the crop is not harmed.

Rosentra controls both grassy and broadleaf weeds in maize, including crowfoot grass, crabgrass, Eleusine and many broadleaf weeds, when sprayed at the early post-emergence stage, typically when weeds have two to four leaves. It is very concentrated, which is why it comes in small 15 ml, 30 ml and 75 ml packs. HPPD herbicides of this type are usually sprayed with an adjuvant to improve uptake.

Use the dose, adjuvant and water volume on the Syngenta label, and spray only on maize.

faqs.a: Topramezone 336 g/L (w/v) SC.
Maize. Do not use it on other crops unless the label lists them.

faqs.q: Why do weeds turn white after spraying?
faqs.a: Topramezone stops the weed making protective pigments, so its leaves bleach in sunlight before it dies. This is the normal sign that it is working.
Early post-emergence, when weeds are young (about two to four leaves). Follow the dose and adjuvant advice on the label.

dS7OVvPKj9yRNX2QbqkS.description:
Confidor Super from Bayer contains imidacloprid 30.5% SC, a systemic neonicotinoid insecticide (IRAC group 4A). The plant absorbs it and carries it to the leaves, so sucking pests that feed on the sap are controlled even on parts the spray did not reach directly. The SC formulation spreads well on the leaf and is absorbed quickly.

Confidor Super is used against aphids, jassids, thrips, whiteflies, brown planthopper and white-backed planthopper in crops such as cotton, paddy and chilli, as listed on the label. These pests suck sap, spread viruses and cause leaf curling and hopper burn, so early control protects yield. The seller's listing gives 60–75 ml per hectare for cotton and paddy; for chilli, follow the current label.

Imidacloprid is highly toxic to bees: avoid spraying flowering crops while bees forage. Rotate with insecticides from other groups to prevent resistance, and follow the waiting period on the Bayer label.

faqs.a: Imidacloprid 30.5% SC.
The listing gives 60–75 ml per hectare for cotton and paddy. For chilli and other crops, follow the current Bayer label.
Sucking pests: aphids, jassids, thrips, whiteflies and planthoppers.
No. Imidacloprid is highly toxic to bees. Do not spray flowering crops while bees are active.

kxFinyTeaSdd1Mwo6Mhj.description:
Delegate from Corteva Agriscience contains spinetoram 11.7% SC, an insecticide from the spinosyn group (IRAC group 5). Spinosyns come from natural soil bacteria and act on the insect's nervous system in a way no other insecticide group does, which makes Delegate valuable for pests that have become resistant to older chemistry.

Delegate controls thrips and caterpillar pests such as fruit borers, diamondback moth and leaf miners in the crops listed on its label, including chilli, onion, brinjal, cabbage and grapes. It works by contact and ingestion and moves into the leaf, so it reaches thrips hiding in folds and on the underside. It has a relatively short waiting period, which suits vegetable crops harvested often.

Spray at the first sign of the pest, with enough water for full coverage. Use it no more than the label allows per season and rotate with other groups. Follow the crop-specific dose on the Corteva label.

faqs.a: Spinetoram 11.7% SC, a spinosyn insecticide.
Thrips and caterpillar pests such as fruit borers, diamondback moth and leaf miners, on the crops listed on its label.
It is crop- and pest-specific. Confirm the rate on the current Indian Corteva label for your crop before spraying.

faqs.q: Why use Delegate when other insecticides fail?
faqs.a: Spinosyns work in a unique way, so they often control thrips and caterpillars that resist older insecticides. Rotate it to keep it effective.

2lUJFSoHMRhY76NzBnvz.description:
OxyFlo from Shivalik contains oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC, a selective herbicide used before weeds come up or just after (pre-emergence and early post-emergence). Oxyfluorfen forms a layer on the soil surface; weed seedlings that emerge through it are burned and die. It also burns young weeds it lands on directly. It belongs to the PPO-inhibitor group.

Oxyfluorfen is widely used in onion and garlic, and in other crops listed on its label such as rice nurseries, groundnut, potato and tea, to control annual broadleaf weeds and some grasses. In onion it is commonly applied soon after transplanting, on moist soil, so the protective layer forms evenly. Do not disturb the soil after spraying, as breaking the layer reduces its effect.

Spray evenly with a flat-fan nozzle and avoid spraying on wet crop foliage, which can cause leaf scorch. Follow the dose and timing on the label for your crop.

faqs.a: Oxyfluorfen 23.5% EC.
Pre-emergence or early post-emergence, on moist soil, as the label directs for your crop. In onion it is usually applied soon after transplanting.
Annual broadleaf weeds such as Chenopodium and Amaranthus, and some annual grasses.
Avoid disturbing the soil for some weeks; breaking the treated layer lets new weeds through.

iK0ZxarcaOyTI4dqNYjx.description:
PLANTO Super Fast is a granular organic fertilizer that combines seaweed extract, humic acid, fulvic acid and amino acids on a bentonite clay granule. Each part does a different job. Humic and fulvic acids improve soil structure and hold nutrients near the roots; seaweed extract supplies natural growth substances and trace elements; amino acids feed the crop and soil microbes; and bentonite helps the soil hold water.

Because it works on the soil as much as on the plant, PLANTO Super Fast is applied at land preparation, at sowing or transplanting, or as a top dressing along the rows, usually mixed with the regular basal fertilizer. It helps young roots establish, improves the response to chemical fertilizers, and supports healthy growth in vegetables, fruit crops, sugarcane, cotton and field crops.

The 50 kg bag suits larger plots. Apply into moist soil or water lightly after application so the granules start to break down. Follow the dose per acre on the bag.

faqs.q: What is in PLANTO Super Fast?
faqs.a: Seaweed extract, humic acid, fulvic acid and amino acids on bentonite granules.
At land preparation, sowing or transplanting, or as a top dressing along the rows, often with the basal fertilizer.
No. It improves the soil and the crop's use of fertilizer, but the crop still needs its NPK.
Yes, it is sold as an organic fertilizer. Follow the dose per acre on the bag.

3kvEQcnsQ5gn8FoqOxn3.description:
Microla from RCF (Rashtriya Chemicals & Fertilizers) is a liquid multi-micronutrient fertilizer containing zinc, iron, copper, boron, molybdenum and manganese. Crops need these elements in small amounts, but a shortage of any one holds back growth even when nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are enough. Typical signs are yellowing between veins, small or distorted new leaves, poor flowering and fruit drop.

As a foliar spray, Microla reaches the leaf directly, which is faster than soil application, especially in alkaline or calcareous soils where micronutrients are locked up. The listing gives 2.5 ml per litre of water for many crop categories; follow the crop-specific directions on the pack. Spray at active vegetative growth and again before flowering for best results.

Microla suits vegetables, fruit crops, pulses, oilseeds and cereals. Test a small mix first before combining it with pesticides in one tank.

faqs.a: Zinc, iron, copper, boron, molybdenum and manganese.
The listing gives 2.5 ml per litre of water for many crops. Follow the crop-specific directions on the pack.
During active vegetative growth and again before flowering, or when deficiency signs appear.

faqs.q: Why spray micronutrients instead of adding them to the soil?
faqs.a: A leaf spray works faster and avoids the lock-up of micronutrients in alkaline soils.

xUVJkpEugG0cucKjjygv.description:
Shahaji Super from Agrimass is a technical-grade super phosphoric acid fertilizer with 115% purity. Super phosphoric acid supplies phosphorus in a highly concentrated, quickly available form. Phosphorus drives root growth, energy transfer inside the plant, flowering and fruit setting, so a timely dose helps young crops establish and mature crops set more flowers and fruit.

The product is promoted for vigorous, long roots and more root hairs, better nutrient uptake, uniform growth, improved flowering and fruit set, longer-lasting green colour, and faster recovery after stress. It suits vegetables such as tomato, chilli, capsicum and cauliflower, field crops such as sugarcane, cotton, soybean and maize, and fruit crops.

Shahaji Super comes in 500 g, 1 kg and 2 kg packs. Because it is acidic and concentrated, measure carefully, dissolve it fully in water, and do not mix it with alkaline products such as lime or copper sprays. Follow the dose and method on the pack.

faqs.a: A technical-grade super phosphoric acid fertilizer (115% purity) that supplies concentrated phosphorus.

faqs.q: What does it do for the crop?
faqs.a: It supports root growth, nutrient uptake, flowering, fruit setting and recovery from stress.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with other sprays?
faqs.a: Avoid mixing it with alkaline products such as lime or copper fungicides. Test a small mix before combining with anything else.
Dissolve it fully in water and apply as the pack directs, by foliar spray or drip.

IgPwtm2su2GhjZlK4suk.description:
Affirm is an insecticide containing emamectin benzoate 5% SG, made for caterpillar pests. Caterpillars that eat treated leaves stop feeding within hours and die over the following days. Emamectin also moves into the leaf (translaminar action), so larvae on the underside of leaves or inside young fruits are reached as well, and the protection lasts for several days.

Affirm is used against fruit and shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth, armyworms, leaf eaters and similar lepidopteran pests in crops such as chilli, tomato, brinjal, okra, cabbage, cotton and pulses, as listed on the label. It works best on young larvae, so spray when eggs are hatching or the first feeding holes appear.

The soluble granules dissolve in water: mix the measured dose in a little water first, then fill the tank. Follow the crop-specific dose and waiting period on the label, and alternate with insecticides from other groups.

faqs.a: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG.
Caterpillars: fruit and shoot borers, bollworms, diamondback moth, armyworms and other leaf-eating larvae.

faqs.q: Does it control whitefly or aphids?
faqs.a: No. It is meant for caterpillars, not sucking pests.

faqs.q: When is the best time to spray?
faqs.a: When young larvae are present, at egg hatch or the first feeding damage.

EQgIehno3xJQeURDBQQd.description:
Humi Gold is a humic acid-based soil conditioner and plant growth enhancer. Humic acid is the active part of well-decomposed organic matter. In the soil it loosens heavy soil and binds light soil, holds water and nutrients near the roots, and feeds soil microbes. In the plant it encourages root branching and better uptake of the fertilizer already applied.

The listing recommends Humi Gold for vegetables, fruits, wheat, rice, pulses and oilseeds, applied by foliar spray or soil drenching, from the early vegetative stage. It is especially useful in soils low in organic matter, in saline or hard soils, and after heavy chemical fertilizer use, where roots struggle.

Humi Gold comes in 250 g and 1 kg packs. Dissolve it fully in water before spraying or drenching. It can be applied with most fertilizers; avoid mixing it with strongly acidic products. Follow the dose on the pack.

faqs.a: It improves soil structure and water holding, supports root development, and helps the crop take up nutrients.
As a foliar spray or soil drench, as listed, starting at the early vegetative stage. Follow the dose on the pack.
Vegetables, fruits, wheat, rice, pulses and oilseeds, according to the listing.
It is a soil conditioner and growth enhancer. It helps fertilizers work better but does not replace NPK.

UuVaAicNvfSy4VgRms8I.description:
The Karan Arjun Onion Tannashak Kit (1 acre) is a ready weed-management program for one acre of onion. Instead of buying several products and working out what to mix, the farmer gets the products for both sprays in one kit, with the order of use written down.

The first spray combines a herbicide against broadleaf weeds (Evenso, oxyfluorfen), a herbicide against grassy weeds (Fusilade), a sticker so the spray spreads and holds on the leaves, and a root booster to help the onion recover and keep growing. Six to eight days later, check the field: if the weeds have dried or burned, the kit includes a second product (Arjuna) for the follow-up spray that supports the crop.

The kit is designed for 10 pumps per acre. Use clean water, spray evenly on a calm day, and read each product's label before mixing. The program is also sold for half an acre and two acres.

faqs.q: What is in the 1 acre kit?
faqs.a: For spray 1: Evenso (oxyfluorfen) herbicide, Fusilade herbicide, a sticker and a root booster. For spray 2: Arjuna, used after checking the field.

faqs.q: When do I do the second spray?
faqs.a: Six to eight days after the first, once you have checked that the weeds have dried or burned.
The kit is designed for 10 pumps per acre.

faqs.q: Is there a smaller or bigger kit?
faqs.a: Yes. The same program is sold for half an acre and for two acres.

MhdOeDTFMn5065FvFeAM.description:
Karan Arjun Power Plus is a plant growth stimulator containing 22% humates and fulvates. Humic and fulvic substances are the active fraction of decomposed organic matter. Applied to the soil or the crop, they encourage new roots and root hairs, hold nutrients and water near the root zone, and help the plant absorb the fertilizer that has been applied, so more of it turns into growth.

The maker describes Power Plus as boosting root growth and nutrient uptake and improving the crop's resistance to drought and disease, for higher yields across crops. It is ISO 9001 certified, each pack carries a QR code to check it is genuine, and the listing says more than 75,800 farmers use it.

Power Plus comes in 1 litre, 3 litre and 5 litre packs. It can be applied through drip, as a soil drench or as a foliar spray, from the early growth stage. Follow the dose on the pack for your crop.

faqs.a: 22% humates and fulvates.
Stronger root growth, better nutrient uptake and better tolerance to drought and disease, for higher yields.

faqs.q: How do I check the pack is genuine?
faqs.a: Each pack carries a QR code for verification.
Through drip, as a soil drench or as a foliar spray, from early growth. Follow the dose on the pack.

cKRF8OP6bOxjvnyWW6Bp.description:
Ampligo from Syngenta is a broad-spectrum insecticide for caterpillar pests, combining chlorantraniliprole 9.3% and lambda-cyhalothrin 4.6% in a ZC formulation. Chlorantraniliprole (IRAC group 28) makes caterpillars stop feeding almost at once and gives long-lasting protection; lambda-cyhalothrin (IRAC group 3A) adds a fast knockdown on contact. The ZC formulation encapsulates part of the active for steadier release.

Ampligo is used against bollworms, stem borers, leaf folders, pod borers and fruit borers in cotton, rice, soybean, pigeon pea (red gram), brinjal and okra. The seller's listing gives these doses: cotton 100 ml per acre, rice 100 ml per acre, soybean 80 ml per acre and pigeon pea 80 ml per acre.

Spray at the first stage of pest infestation, covering the crop well. Ampligo is toxic to bees and fish; avoid spraying flowering crops while bees forage and keep it away from water bodies. Follow the waiting period on the Syngenta label.

faqs.a: Chlorantraniliprole 9.3% plus lambda-cyhalothrin 4.6% ZC.

faqs.q: What is the dose per acre?
faqs.a: From the listing: cotton 100 ml, rice 100 ml, soybean 80 ml and pigeon pea 80 ml per acre. Follow the label for other crops.
Caterpillars such as bollworms, stem borers, leaf folders, pod borers and fruit borers.
At the initial stage of pest infestation, as directed on the label.

5c34OUjfWHWqGVoEew59.description:
Amistar from Syngenta contains azoxystrobin 23% SC, a broad-spectrum systemic fungicide from the strobilurin group. Azoxystrobin stops fungal spores from germinating and blocks the fungus's energy supply. It moves into the leaf and spreads across it, so it protects areas next to where the drop landed, and it has a mild greening effect that helps the crop stay healthy longer.

Amistar controls powdery mildew, downy mildew, anthracnose, blight and similar diseases in the crops on its label, including grapes, chilli, tomato, potato, rice and others. It works best as a preventive spray, or at the first signs of disease, because strobilurins stop infection before it takes hold.

To keep azoxystrobin effective, do not use it in back-to-back sprays: alternate it with fungicides from other groups and follow the maximum number of sprays on the label. Use the dose and spray interval on the Syngenta label for your crop.

faqs.q: What is the active ingredient in Amistar?
faqs.a: Azoxystrobin 23% SC.
Powdery mildew, downy mildew, anthracnose, blight and other fungal diseases on the crops listed on its label.

faqs.q: How is Amistar different from Amistar Top?
faqs.a: Amistar has azoxystrobin alone. Amistar Top adds difenoconazole, which gives extra curative action.

faqs.q: How often can I spray it?
faqs.a: Follow the label's maximum number of sprays and alternate with fungicides from other groups.

8WIedwwqkOTZrERPsS7W.description:
Calaris Xtra from Syngenta is a selective, systemic post-emergence herbicide for maize and sugarcane, containing mesotrione 2.27% w/w and atrazine 22.7% w/w SC. The two actives work in different ways: mesotrione bleaches weeds by blocking pigment production, and atrazine stops photosynthesis. Together they control both grassy and broadleaf weeds with a fast knockdown and long-lasting effect.

Spray Calaris Xtra when the weeds are at the three to four leaf stage. The seller's listing gives 1,400 ml per acre in 200 litres of water, and it is sold in 350 ml, 700 ml and 1,400 ml packs. Use a flat-fan nozzle and walk at a steady pace for even coverage.

Calaris Xtra is for maize and sugarcane only. Atrazine stays in the soil for some time, so check the label before planting a sensitive crop in the same field afterwards. Follow the Syngenta label for timing and safety.

faqs.a: Mesotrione 2.27% w/w plus atrazine 22.7% w/w SC.
The listing gives 1,400 ml per acre in 200 litres of water, sprayed at the 3–4 leaf stage of weeds.

faqs.q: Which crops can I use it on?
faqs.a: Maize (corn) and sugarcane.
Both grassy and broadleaf weeds, when sprayed at the young stage.

ozuCUS1Ar26Z0zuviI3B.description:
Fertistar 16:16:12 is a liquid NPK complex fertilizer with 16% nitrogen, 16% phosphorus and 12% potassium. With equal nitrogen and phosphorus and a little less potassium, it is made for the early and middle stages of the crop, when the plant is building leaves, roots and branches and needs a balanced, quick feed.

It can be sprayed on the leaves for a fast effect, or given through drip, and it supplements the basal fertilizer applied at sowing. Common uses are in vegetables after transplanting, in field crops during vegetative growth, and in fruit crops after pruning, when new growth starts. Foliar feeding is especially useful when the soil is dry or cold and roots cannot take up nutrients well.

Fertistar 16:16:12 comes in 500 ml and 1 litre packs. Shake well, spray in the morning or evening, and follow the dose on the pack for your crop and stage.

faqs.a: 16% nitrogen, 16% phosphorus and 12% potassium.

faqs.q: At what stage should I use it?
faqs.a: Early to mid growth: vegetative growth, root and branch development.

faqs.q: Can I use it through drip?
faqs.a: Yes, it can be used as a foliar spray or through drip. Follow the dose on the pack.
No. It supplements the fertilizer applied at sowing.

5U7Agf1D6bGICw77qj3P.description:
UNI ROOT KING is a humic acid-based biostimulant made with potassium humate. Potassium humate dissolves fully in water and brings the benefits of humic acid to the root zone: more and longer roots, better soil structure, higher water-holding capacity, and better uptake of nutrients, especially phosphorus and micronutrients that are otherwise locked in the soil.

The listing gives a dose of 1 kg per hectare, applied to the soil or through fertigation (drip), at transplanting, flowering, fruit setting and ripening. It also helps seed germination and early crop vigour, and is useful in soils low in organic matter or damaged by salts. UNI ROOT KING suits vegetables, fruit crops, sugarcane and field crops.

It comes as a 1 kg pack of potassium humate powder with a shelf life of up to three years from manufacture. Dissolve the powder fully in water before applying it through drip, so it does not block the emitters.

faqs.q: What does UNI ROOT KING contain?
faqs.a: Humic acid as potassium humate powder.
The listing gives 1 kg per hectare, by soil application or fertigation.
At transplanting, flowering, fruit setting and ripening, according to the listing.

faqs.q: Can I put it through drip?
faqs.a: Yes. Dissolve it fully in water first so it does not block the emitters.

2x5iA8nPGfjbY3K4BGcG.description:
Vibrance Integral from Syngenta is a seed treatment that protects seed and seedlings from both fungal diseases and insect pests. It contains three actives: sedaxane 12.61% w/w and azoxystrobin 3.15% w/w against seed- and soil-borne fungi, and thiamethoxam 22.06% w/w against early insect pests. It is an FS (flowable concentrate for seed treatment), applied to the seed before sowing, not sprayed on the crop.

Sedaxane is known for protecting young roots against Rhizoctonia and similar fungi, which helps the seedling build a larger, healthier root system. Azoxystrobin widens the disease protection, and thiamethoxam moves into the seedling to control sucking and soil insects in the first weeks. The result is an even stand and a strong start.

Treat the seed evenly using the crop-specific rate and method on the current Indian label. Do not use foliar-spray doses. Dry treated seed in the shade before sowing, keep it away from food and feed, and wash hands after handling.

faqs.a: Sedaxane 12.61% w/w, azoxystrobin 3.15% w/w and thiamethoxam 22.06% w/w FS.
As a seed treatment before sowing, at the crop-specific rate on the label. It is not a foliar spray.
Seed- and soil-borne fungal diseases and early-season insect pests.

faqs.q: Can treated seed be used as food or feed?
faqs.a: No. Keep treated seed away from food and animal feed.

ioZAwU2JXgRQztXHlKXW.description:
JEFHA MAX PRO is a universal dispersant for water-soluble fertilizers and micronutrients. Many soluble fertilizers form lumps or leave sediment in the tank, especially in hard or cold water, which blocks nozzles and drip emitters and means part of the nutrient never reaches the crop. A dispersant keeps the particles separated so they dissolve quickly and evenly.

The listing gives 50 ml per 200 litres of water, for both drip irrigation and foliar spray. Add JEFHA MAX PRO to the water first, then add the fertilizer and stir. The result is faster, uniform dissolution, no lumps or settling, cleaner equipment, and better use of the fertilizer you have paid for.

JEFHA MAX PRO comes in 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre packs. It is a tank-mix aid, not a fertilizer itself, and can be used with most water-soluble fertilizers and micronutrient mixes. Follow the instructions on the pack.

faqs.q: What does JEFHA MAX PRO do?
faqs.a: It helps water-soluble fertilizers and micronutrients dissolve quickly and evenly, without lumps or sediment.
The listing gives 50 ml per 200 litres of water.

faqs.q: Can I use it in drip?
faqs.a: Yes, it is made for both drip irrigation and foliar spray.
No. It is a dispersant that helps fertilizers work better.

N6Ee4vbvbA3fpwc6QjH9.description:
Folio Gold from Syngenta is a broad-spectrum fungicide in suspension concentrate (SC) form that combines systemic and contact action. It is widely used against downy mildew and blight. The systemic part, metalaxyl-M, moves inside the plant and stops infection that has already begun, while the contact part, chlorothalonil, forms a protective layer on the leaf that stops spores germinating.

The listing describes Folio Gold as applied by foliar spray or soil drenching, typically at 2 ml per litre of water, and as forming a protective layer on the canopy while acting inside the plant. It is used in vegetables such as tomato, potato, chilli and cucurbits, in grapes and in other crops listed on the label, especially in humid weather when downy mildew and late blight spread fast.

Folio Gold is a fungicide, not a fertilizer. Spray preventively or at the first symptoms, and alternate with fungicides from other groups. Follow the Syngenta label for crops and waiting periods.

faqs.q: What type of product is Folio Gold?
faqs.a: A systemic plus contact fungicide in SC form. It is not a fertilizer.
The listing gives 2 ml per litre of water. Follow the crop-specific label.
Mainly downy mildew and blights caused by oomycetes, on the crops listed on its label.
Preventively in humid weather, or at the first symptoms.

27mIHDRYlKT60guaRx9A.description:
LOTUS Hybrid Maize Seed (Shivam Lotus, Abhiruchi-449) is a hybrid maize with a yield potential of up to 56 quintals per acre and a maturity period of 105 to 110 days. It can be grown in kharif, rabi and summer, and the listing names a wide range of suitable states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

The seed is chosen for good germination and strong crop establishment. Sow it in well-drained, fertile soil at the spacing on the pack, apply phosphorus and potassium at sowing, and split the nitrogen between sowing, knee height and pre-tasselling. Keep the crop weed-free for the first five to six weeks and make sure it has water at tasselling and silking, when stress costs the most yield.

Scout early for fall armyworm in the whorls. As with all hybrids, buy fresh seed each season. Each pack holds 4 kg.

faqs.q: What is the yield potential of LOTUS maize?
faqs.a: Up to 56 quintals per acre, according to the listing.

faqs.q: How long does it take to mature?
faqs.a: 105 to 110 days.

faqs.q: In which seasons can I grow it?
faqs.a: Kharif, rabi and summer.

faqs.q: Can I save the seed for next season?
faqs.a: No. It is a hybrid; buy fresh seed each season.

JNkwH4YBHDO198x9sqR6.description:
Tekko contains quizalofop ethyl 5% EC, a selective herbicide that kills grassy weeds without harming broadleaf crops. It is used in onion to control shipat and other grassy weeds. Quizalofop is absorbed by the leaves and moves to the growing points of the grass, where it stops the weed making fats for new cells; the grass stops growing within days and turns yellow to brown over one to two weeks.

Spray Tekko after the grassy weeds have come up, when they are young and actively growing, ideally at the two to five leaf stage. Onion and other broadleaf crops listed on the label are not affected. Tekko does not control broadleaf weeds or sedges such as motha, so a separate herbicide is needed for those.

Spray on a calm day with a flat-fan nozzle, and avoid spraying just before rain or on weeds stressed by drought. Follow the dose on the label.

faqs.a: Quizalofop ethyl 5% EC.
Grassy weeds, such as shipat in onion. It does not control broadleaf weeds or motha.

faqs.q: Will it harm my onion crop?
faqs.a: No. Onion is a broadleaf crop and is not affected when Tekko is used as the label directs.
Post-emergence, when the grassy weeds are young and actively growing.

MX1qejjOq65ntRZGPBQv.description:
FASTER from UNIMAX is an organic silicon-based adjuvant: a wetting, spreading, penetrating and dispersing agent added to pesticide and fertilizer sprays. Water droplets on waxy leaves bead up and roll off. A silicon surfactant lowers the surface tension, so each drop spreads into a thin film that covers much more of the leaf and sticks to it.

Better coverage and penetration mean the pesticide or fertilizer in the tank works better, often at the same dose. FASTER is 100% water soluble, neutral in pH and compatible with most tank mixes, and it suits all field crops, vegetables, fruits, pulses, oilseeds and horticultural crops. It is especially useful on waxy-leaved crops such as onion, cabbage and chilli, and in sprays where coverage decides the result.

FASTER comes in packs from 50 ml to 1 litre. Add it to the tank last, after the other products are mixed, and follow the dose on the pack.

faqs.a: It helps spray droplets spread, stick and penetrate, so pesticides and fertilizers cover the leaf better.

faqs.q: Which crops can I use it on?
faqs.a: All field crops, vegetables, fruits, pulses, oilseeds and horticultural crops.

faqs.q: When do I add it to the tank?
faqs.a: Last, after the pesticide or fertilizer is mixed.

i7AwKKxFU8EcQeLn5Z18.description:
Topra is a selective post-emergence herbicide based on topramezone, for controlling grasses and broadleaf weeds in maize. Topramezone stops the weed making the pigments that protect its leaves, so new leaves turn white in sunlight and the weed dies within one to two weeks. Maize breaks the active down quickly and is not harmed.

The listing gives a dose of 75–100 ml per hectare of the formulation, plus an MSO adjuvant at 2 ml per litre of water, sprayed at the early post-emergence stage when weeds are at the two to three leaf stage. It controls grasses such as Eleusine indica (crowfoot), Digitaria sanguinalis (crabgrass) and Dactyloctenium, as well as broadleaf weeds.

Topra is very concentrated, which is why it comes in 15 ml and 30 ml packs. Measure accurately, use the recommended adjuvant, and spray only on maize.

faqs.q: What is the dose of Topra?
faqs.a: The listing gives 75–100 ml per hectare plus MSO adjuvant at 2 ml per litre of water.
Maize.
Early post-emergence, when weeds are at the 2–3 leaf stage.

faqs.q: Why do the weeds turn white?
faqs.a: Topramezone stops pigment production, so leaves bleach before the weed dies. This shows the herbicide is working.

olPa617Vh8qf6CxS1vl2.description:
EverGol Xtend from Bayer is a seed-treatment fungicide for soybean and groundnut. It combines penflufen and trifloxystrobin, two fungicides with different modes of action, to protect the seed and young seedling against seed- and soil-borne diseases such as collar rot, root rot and seedling blight. Healthy seedlings give an even stand and a stronger root system from the start.

Seed treatment uses far less fungicide than spraying the field, because it puts the active exactly where the disease attacks: on the seed and around the young root. The listing notes that EverGol Xtend supports root development and better crop establishment when used as directed.

Treat the seed evenly before sowing at the crop-specific rate on the current Indian label; do not use foliar-spray doses. Dry treated seed in the shade, sow it soon after treatment, and keep it away from food and animal feed.

faqs.q: Which crops is EverGol Xtend for?
faqs.a: Soybean and groundnut seed treatment.
Seed- and soil-borne diseases that attack the seed and seedling, such as collar rot and root rot.
Treat the seed uniformly before sowing at the rate on the label. It is not a foliar spray.

faqs.q: Can treated seed be fed to animals?
faqs.a: No. Keep treated seed away from food and feed.

Q4dzkbRUPZWKCJe0kLpW.description:
Aliette from Bayer contains fosetyl-Al 80% WP, a systemic fungicide that is unusual in moving both up and down inside the plant, to the roots as well as new shoots. It is used against oomycete diseases: downy mildew in grapes, damping-off in tomato and cardamom nurseries, and azhukal (capsule rot) in cardamom. Fosetyl-Al also triggers the plant's own defences, which adds to its protective effect.

The seller's listing gives these doses: grapes 1.4–2 kg per hectare and cardamom 2.25–3 kg per hectare; for tomato, follow the current product label. Depending on the crop and disease, it is applied as a foliar spray or as a seedling drench.

Because it moves to the roots, Aliette protects parts of the plant the spray cannot reach. Do not mix it with copper fungicides or foliar fertilizers containing copper. Follow the spray interval and waiting period on the Bayer label.

faqs.a: Fosetyl-Al 80% WP.
From the listing: grapes 1.4–2 kg per hectare and cardamom 2.25–3 kg per hectare. For tomato, follow the current label.
Downy mildew in grapes, damping-off in tomato and cardamom, and azhukal disease in cardamom.

faqs.q: Can I mix it with copper sprays?
faqs.a: No. Do not mix Aliette with copper fungicides or copper-containing fertilizers.

pUASTXRBVgwJL3jU8LD8.description:
Cymbush contains cypermethrin 25% EC, a broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroid insecticide. It acts on contact and as a stomach poison, attacking the insect's nervous system and giving a quick knockdown. Cypermethrin is widely used against chewing pests such as bollworms, fruit borers, caterpillars and beetles, and some sucking pests, in the crops listed on its label.

Because it works mainly on contact, good coverage is essential: spray both sides of the leaves and the parts of the plant where the pest feeds. Spray at the first sign of the pest, in the morning or evening. Pyrethroids lose effect if used too often, so alternate Cymbush with insecticides from other groups.

Cypermethrin is poisonous. Wear gloves, a mask and long sleeves when mixing and spraying, do not eat or smoke while working, and keep it away from ponds and wells, as it is very toxic to fish. Follow the crop-specific dose on the approved label; there is no single dose for all crops.

faqs.a: Cypermethrin 25% EC.
Chewing pests such as bollworms, fruit borers, caterpillars and beetles, and some sucking pests, on the crops listed on its label.

P0gAh9ME8UucrIQq9exh.description:
Thyro Super contains abamectin 1.9% EC, an insecticide and acaricide (miticide). Abamectin acts on contact and when eaten, and it moves into the leaf (translaminar action), forming a reservoir inside the leaf tissue. Mites and insects feeding on the underside of leaves are controlled even though the spray landed on the top.

Abamectin is best known for controlling red spider mites and two-spotted mites, and it also controls leaf miners and some other pests in the crops on its label, such as roses, grapes and vegetables. Mites multiply very fast in hot, dry weather, so spray as soon as you see stippling or webbing on the leaves, and cover the undersides well.

The listing notes published label rates for abamectin 1.9% EC, such as 0.75 ml per litre for grapes, but asks you to confirm Thyro Super's own approved label before using any rate. Rotate with acaricides from other groups to avoid resistance.

faqs.a: Abamectin 1.9% EC.
Mites, such as red spider mites, and other labelled insect pests such as leaf miners.
It is crop-specific. Confirm the rate on Thyro Super's own approved label before applying.

faqs.q: How do I get the best control of mites?
faqs.a: Spray at the first signs of mite damage and cover the underside of the leaves well.

BbwxgFutohTpNp5qzmo8.description:
Cabrio Top from BASF is a broad-spectrum fungicide containing metiram 55% and pyraclostrobin 5% WG. Metiram is a multi-site contact fungicide that protects the leaf surface; pyraclostrobin is a strobilurin that enters the leaf and stops the fungus producing energy. The combination gives both protective action and longer-lasting control, and it lowers the risk of resistance.

Cabrio Top is used against diseases such as downy mildew, anthracnose, leaf spots and blights in grapes, chilli, onion, tomato, potato and pomegranate, as listed. Pyraclostrobin also supports leaf health, which helps crop quality and yield. Spray preventively when weather favours disease, or at the first symptoms, and repeat at the interval on the label.

The water-dispersible granules mix easily without dust; pour them into a partly filled tank while stirring. Cabrio Top comes in a 600 g pack. Follow the BASF label for the dose and waiting period on your crop.

faqs.a: Metiram 55% plus pyraclostrobin 5% WG.

faqs.q: Which crops is it used on?
faqs.a: Grapes, chilli, onion, tomato, potato and pomegranate, among others listed.
Downy mildew, anthracnose, leaf spots, blights and other listed fungal diseases.

h4I0A77HaUpnpFkoIbGX.description:
Crystal Gramoxone contains paraquat dichloride 24% SL, a fast-acting, non-selective contact herbicide. It kills the green parts of any plant it touches by disrupting photosynthesis; weeds start to wilt within hours in sunlight and dry out in a day or two. It does not move into the roots, so it burns down the top growth of weeds rather than killing deep-rooted perennials.

Paraquat is used to clear annual grasses and broadleaf weeds before sowing, between crop rows with a shield, on bunds and in plantations, only where the registered label allows. It becomes inactive on contact with soil, so it leaves no soil residue for the next crop.

Paraquat is highly toxic to people if swallowed, and there is no antidote. Never store it in drink bottles, keep it locked away from children, wear gloves, a mask and eye protection while mixing and spraying, and do not spray in windy weather. Follow the dose and uses on the registered label.

faqs.a: Paraquat dichloride 24% SL.

cRNQHZAlYDa1RF26swwl.description:
SWAL CANORA EZ contains clethodim 13% w/w EC, a selective post-emergence herbicide for grassy weeds in cotton, soybean and onion. Clethodim is an ACCase inhibitor: it stops grass weeds producing the fats they need for new cells, so they stop growing within days and die over one to two weeks. Broadleaf crops are not affected.

The listing names the grasses it controls: jungle rice (Echinochloa colona), large crabgrass (Digitaria sanguinalis), running grass (Brachiaria reptans), viper grass (Dinebra arabica), crowfoot grass (Dactyloctenium aegyptium), goosegrass (Eleusine indica) and Bermuda grass. Spray when the grasses are young and actively growing.

Canora EZ does not control broadleaf weeds or sedges, so plan a separate herbicide for those if needed. Spray on a calm day, avoid rain soon after spraying, and follow the registered label for the dose and water volume.

faqs.q: What does SWAL CANORA EZ contain?
faqs.a: Clethodim 13% w/w EC.

faqs.q: Which crops can I use it on?
faqs.a: Cotton, soybean and onion.
Grassy weeds, including jungle rice, crabgrass, crowfoot grass, goosegrass and Bermuda grass.

unb6QweynV1zQTNLtGXB.description:
ARJUN ASTRA-54 is a 100% water-soluble potash (potassium) fertilizer. Potassium is the nutrient of fruit and grain quality: it moves sugars into fruits and grains, builds fruit size, colour and shine, strengthens cell walls and helps the plant manage water. Crops with enough potassium also handle disease and dry spells better.

The listing gives the dose as 2–3 ml per litre of water for foliar spray and 2–4 ml per litre for drip irrigation, and lists vegetable crops such as tomato, chilli, brinjal, bitter gourd and okra, and fruit crops such as apple, grapes and mango. Use it mainly from flowering onward, through fruit setting and fruit development.

ARJUN ASTRA-54 comes in 500 g, 1 kg and 2 kg packs. Spray in the morning or evening, and test a small mix first before combining it with pesticides in one tank.

faqs.a: Potassium (potash) in a fully water-soluble form.
The listing gives 2–3 ml per litre for foliar spray and 2–4 ml per litre for drip.
From flowering through fruit setting and fruit development.
